topics.topic: Lifecycle state and activation behavior of implicitly created manual BudgetVersion
questions: In which lifecycle state is the implicitly created manual budget version, and does its creation count as activation?
What lifecycle state and activation provenance must the lazily created manual budget version have?
What status does the implicit manual version receive, and what happens if another budget version is already active?

judgement.why: This is the same question previously decided by P4, and neither the deciding later-state text nor the relevant passages have changed.

precedent.topic: Lifecycle state and activation provenance of the implicitly created manual BudgetVersion
quotes:
A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).
precedent.why: State 5 makes the implicitly created manual version inactive and forbids implicit activation, so activation metadata is not populated by this creation.

topics.topic: Transaction commit or rollback semantics for side-effecting list_project_progress
questions: Is list_project_progress a committing write path despite being a read, or must the read-path rollback rule apply to it?
Is list_project_progress a write path that commits its lazy budget creation, or a read path whose transaction is rolled back?
Must this operation use the write-path commit protocol when it performs implicit creation, or must it still follow the read-path rollback protocol?

judgement.why: This is the same transaction-treatment question previously decided by P8, and neither the deciding later-state text nor the relevant passages have changed.

precedent.topic: Commit versus rollback treatment of the side-effecting progress read
quotes:
The tracking read transaction closes before
`budget_management.ensure_manual_budget` is called for the order.

Writes one `BudgetVersion` and one `AuditRecord` when none exists; otherwise
read-only.

Not a pure read: when the project has no manual budget version, this list
creates it empty with its `budget.manual_version_create` audit, exactly as
`ensure_manual_budget` does, an archived project included; otherwise
read-only.
precedent.why: State 5 closes the tracking read transaction before invoking a separate operation that commits the manual version and audit, so the created records are not rolled back as read-path work.

topics.topic: Validation and UTC normalization of caller-supplied ServiceCredential.expires_at
questions: Which supplied service-credential expiry values must be refused—for example an expiry equal to now, already in the past, or unreasonably far in the future?
What happens when a caller supplies an offset-aware expiry or an expiry expressed with a non-UTC offset?
Which supplied service-credential expiry values are valid, and must an offset-bearing instant be rejected or normalized before persistence?
Must credential issuance reject an expiry equal to or before the operation instant, and what UTC representation is accepted before storing the required offset-naive value?

judgement.why: This is the same validation and normalization question previously decided by P2, and neither the deciding later-state text nor the relevant passages have changed.

precedent.topic: Validation and normalization rules for supplied ServiceCredential.expires_at
quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.
precedent.why: State 5 accepts any supplied expiry, including a past or offset-bearing value, preserves it without conversion, and makes an already-reached expiry immediately unusable.

topics.topic: Whether supplied credential expiry is preserved or constrained to operation time plus TTL
questions: Does the instant-plus-TTL invariant exclude a supplied ServiceCredential.expires_at, or must credential issuance replace or constrain the supplied value to a TTL-derived value?
When an administrator supplies a service credential expires_at, must the stored value remain the supplied instant or be replaced by operation_now plus a TTL?
Does a service credential retain the supplied `expires_at`, or must its persisted expiry equal the operation clock plus a configured TTL?

judgement.why: This is the same supplied-versus-derived credential-expiry question previously decided by P6, and neither the deciding later-state text nor the relevant passages have changed.

precedent.topic: Whether ServiceCredential.expires_at is preserved or derived from operation time and TTL
quotes:
The `PortalStore`, the administrator's `StaffActorContext`, the principal id
and an optional `expires_at`. Any expiry is accepted and stored as
supplied, a past one included, never converted (A28 keeps a supplied time); no expiry means the credential does not expire. A
credential is usable only before its expiry, so one issued with an expiry
already reached is stored but never authenticates.
precedent.why: State 5 explicitly preserves the request-supplied optional expiry and defines no service-credential TTL derivation.

precedent.topic: Authorization of implicit manual-version creation during archived-project progress reads
quotes:
The one write that is not refused for an archived project
is the empty manual budget version (with its audit) that
`ensure_manual_budget` creates, also when `list_project_progress` reads a
project that has none.

Not a pure read: when the project has no manual budget version, this list
creates it empty with its `budget.manual_version_create` audit, exactly as
`ensure_manual_budget` does, an archived project included; otherwise
read-only.
precedent.why: State 5 explicitly authorizes the archived project as a read and permits the exceptional manual-version write and audit.

topics.topic: Concurrency handling for races between first progress reads creating a budget
questions: How must concurrent first progress reads resolve the creation race?

judgement.why: This is the same concurrent manual-version creation question previously decided by P5, and neither the deciding later-state text nor the relevant passages have changed.

precedent.topic: Required outcome of concurrent implicit manual-version creation races
quotes:
A18: at most one manual version per project; a new one is `inactive` and is
never activated implicitly; A13 (`budget.manual_version_create` only when it
is created).
precedent.why: State 5 enforces uniqueness through persistence and permits a racing request to fail because the resulting persistence failure propagates rather than being retried or converted into success.
